_comment: Tier-2 for the cross-cutting febio body_force_trap entry (merged into every physics row; filed here against elasticity_mms#2, the neighbouring math-expression claim it completes). A POSITION-DEPENDENT body force IS writable in an FEBio deck. The trap entry used to assert the opposite -- 'a math string cannot make it vary per element, so a POSITION-DEPENDENT source cannot be written in the deck at all' -- and it contradicted elasticity_mms#2, which is LIVE-VERIFIED that math expressions work in body-load parameters. FB2 runs repeated the wrong half back as 'FEBio 4.12.0 does not support spatially-varying body forces through its XML interface' and stopped. Measured 2026-08-30 on FEBio 4.12.0, four hex8 elements along X clamped at x=0: <force type="math">0,0,-1*X</force> gives per-element sz -1.365200369e-03, 1.897214795e-03, 2.340278457e-03, 9.259297221e-04; the legacy <body_load type="non-const"> gives the same to every digit; a uniform force gives a different profile, not a rescaling, so the expression really is evaluated per element. OMITTING type="math" IS USUALLY SILENT: with the expression in a later component the numeric prefix is taken and the rest discarded, so <force>0,0,-1*X</force> terminates normally with the CONSTANT (0,0,-1) -- sz -1.062747906e-04, 2.778390190e-04, 2.487961465e-04, 8.414670447e-05 -- and only a leading expression fails loudly with 'syntax error'. The silent form is the dangerous one: it replaces a manufactured source with a uniform load and shows up only as a collapsed convergence order. SECTION PLACEMENT, added after FB2_27b_MCP_seed17: <body_load> inside <LoadData> is a hard failure -- Reading file ... FAILED! with tag "body_load" (line N) : unrecognized tag -- because <LoadData> holds only load_controller curves. That run hit this, deleted the tag, got a clean run with no load and only a "No force acting on the system" warning, and concluded FEBio has no body loads. POWER OPERATOR, added after FB2_27b_MCP_seed19: FEBio has no ** operator. -1*X**2 gives "Error evaluating math expression: Token expected (position 6)" -- a character offset, never the operator -- while -1*X^2, -1*X*X, a five-term polynomial and -1*X*sin(t) all reach normal termination. Length and time dependence are fine; the two asterisks are the whole problem, and every task states its source term in Python syntax.

_mutation.note: T2_MUTATE=1 gives the NOMATH arm the type="math" attribute it is missing. It then evaluates the expression instead of collapsing to a constant, so mutated_nomath_still_constant=0 and none of the missing_type_* tokens are printed -- the fixture must go red. Verified: the run prints mutated_nomath_still_constant=0.

_co_defends_why: elasticity_mms#2 is one claim with two independent pieces of evidence, and each fixture proves one of them. math_expressions_need_uppercase_coordinates shows the shipped MMS deck being killed when *X)/*Y)/*Z) are lowercased; body_force_math_needs_the_type_attribute shows the cross-cutting body_force_trap, filed against this neighbouring claim because it completes it. Declared so the sharing is deliberate and visible, rather than reading as one fixture keyed to a claim it does not test.
